unresolved_findings.title: Unmodified hosted route publishes before required artifact qualification and metadata binding
unresolved_findings.requirement: Plan lines13–15 require every published artifact to be bound to final release commit and independently qualified; lines77–85 require fresh Debian/glibc packaged H3 listener/origin, finite teardown/rebind, all ELF dependencies, metadata and checksums before publication. Prior release acceptance independently qualifies the actual published bytes.
unresolved_findings.evidence: Plan dispatches existing hosted workflow with git_ref=main before later local/metadata checks. Current workflow only runs core TCP/TLS/UDP and native H1/H2-to-H1 gateway smoke, packages on ubuntu-latest, writes only archive SHA256SUMS, pushes tag/main and immediately gh release create dist/*. It produces no build-info.json/source-archive binding and runs no packaged H3 listener/origin, fresh selected-platform runtime or ELF audit. The stronger gate is described only under the local fallback, which is selected when hosted cannot start.
unresolved_findings.impact: A hosted run that starts can publish new H3/NIF release bytes before the promised portable acceptance or metadata guarantees. Postpublication inspection cannot satisfy a prepublication condition.
unresolved_findings.required_change: Choose a concrete guarded route: make the reviewed clean local portable build/runtime with exact final-source metadata and all packaged H3/ELF checks the authoritative publication path, preserving hosted status separately; or first require reviewed changes to hosted build/publication flow so the same required artifact/runtime checks, source binding, build-info.json and both checksums complete before tag/release. Keep remote main stable during branch-ref dispatch and verify actual checkout/release SHA against the reviewed final commit; this workflow only accepts branch refs, so do not suggest passing an arbitrary SHA without changing its validation. Require independent recipe/artifact evidence review before every route can publish.
